sugestoes.texto: Each new strategy reuses the factory's queue_pool even though SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() permanently shuts that pool down. Arroyo closes and recreates strategies during rebalances without reconstructing the factory, so the next strategy submits into shut-down queues; submit catches the resulting exception and marks those unprocessed messages complete, allowing their offsets to be committed. Create a fresh pool and offset tracker for each strategy assignment rather than reusing a pool destroyed by the previous strategy.

close() stops the commit thread and shuts workers down before accepted work has drained, while join() only calls close() again. FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown immediately, so a worker exits after its current item with queued items remaining, and work finishing after the commit thread exits has no final commit; during rebalance this abandons accepted work and replays completed work, with slow workers potentially continuing after ownership is released. Make close stop new submissions, and make join drain queued and in-flight work within its timeout and commit the final completed offsets before shutting workers down.

The worker queues are unbounded and the strategy never rejects submissions to apply backpressure. When a subscription's worker is slow or aggregate processing falls behind Kafka consumption, the consumer keeps retaining WorkItems containing both decoded results and original messages, along with offset sets, until process memory is exhausted. Bound total pending work and reject submissions with Arroyo's MessageRejected when capacity is exhausted, ensuring rejected messages are not caught and marked complete by the broad submit exception handler.

The factory reuses self.queue_pool across strategy instances, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() and terminate() in queue_consumer.py permanently shut that pool down. When a partition reassignment closes the old strategy and creates a replacement from this factory, the replacement gets the same stopped workers and shut-down queues. Submissions then fail (and the strategy's exception handler marks those offsets complete), allowing results to be skipped without processing. Give each strategy a fresh pool, or explicitly keep the shared pool alive across strategy replacement with appropriate draining and offset-state isolation.

The documented guarantee says offsets are committed only after successful processing, but OrderedQueueWorker.run catches processor exceptions and unconditionally calls complete_offset in finally. The commit loop therefore also commits failed items (and submit similarly marks decoding/grouping failures complete). Document the actual discard-on-error policy rather than promising successful delivery; callers choosing this strategy otherwise receive a false reliability contract.

FixedQueuePool constructs queue.Queue() with its default unbounded capacity, and submit always puts the item without any capacity check or rejection. These queues never fill up in the sense required to provide backpressure. Remove this guarantee or explicitly describe the unbounded buffering so callers do not rely on this strategy to limit queued memory when processing falls behind.

If result_processor raises (for example during a transient database failure), the exception is logged but the finally block removes its offset from outstanding. The commit thread can then commit this offset and all subsequent completed work, permanently skipping the failed result on restart. This violates the strategy's declared successful-processing-only commit guarantee. Preserve the failed offset and propagate the failure to the strategy or retry it before allowing commits past it.

The pool belongs to ResultsStrategyFactory and create_thread_queue_parallel_worker passes that same pool to every new strategy. Closing the current strategy shuts down its queues and workers permanently, but leaves factory.queue_pool pointing to it. When a partition reassignment creates the next strategy, submission to those shut-down queues raises; submit catches that error and marks the message complete, so the consumer can commit results it never processed. Create a fresh pool for each strategy lifetime, or keep the shared pool alive until factory shutdown with appropriate draining and tracker reset.

This test submits five identical decoded results and only asserts their count. Processing them in reverse order would still pass. Give each message a distinguishable value while retaining the same grouping key, then assert the exact processed sequence.

Waiting for six completions and checking that three group names appeared establishes eventual processing, not concurrency. A pool that routes every group to one worker passes this test. Use distinct known queues and events or a barrier to establish that a second processor enters while the first remains blocked.

The worker marks even failed items complete in its finally block, but this test sleeps only 0.2 seconds after processing and then accepts no commits. The commit loop waits 1 second, so the test can pass before the erroneous commit occurs. Synchronize on an actual commit-loop iteration after both processing attempts and then assert the intended offset behavior.

Checking factory.queue_pool is None does not verify graceful shutdown. The factory clears that attribute regardless of whether queued items were drained or worker threads stopped; the current pool sets worker.shutdown before draining, so queued work can be abandoned while this test passes. Retain the pool reference, track submitted results, and assert all are processed and all workers have exited after shutdown.

complete_offset runs in finally even when result_processor raises. A transient processing failure at offset 100 followed by successful processing at 101 therefore makes both offsets committable, permanently skipping the failed result on restart. Only mark successful processing complete, and propagate or retry worker failures rather than treating them as success.

The pool is constructed once in the factory, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close shuts that pool down. When a partition reassignment creates a replacement strategy using the same factory, this code hands it the same stopped workers and shut-down queues. Submissions can then fail and be marked complete by the submission exception handler without ever being processed. Give each strategy a fresh pool, or keep pool lifecycle exclusively at the factory level with appropriate offset-state reset.

Setting worker.shutdown before calling queue.shutdown(immediate=False) defeats the drain behavior: run checks the flag before fetching each item, so a busy worker exits after its current item and leaves the rest queued. Normal close/join consequently returns without processing accepted work. For graceful shutdown, let workers keep consuming until get raises queue.ShutDown after the queue is drained; reserve immediate stopping for termination.

issues.descricao: Claims OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets requires every integer offset to exist, so Kafka offset gaps permanently block commits for the partition and per-partition state is never cleared on rebalance.

comentarios.texto: Offsets are only tracked for messages that were submitted, and there is no partition revoke handling. Contiguity is checked with `range(start, max_offset+1)`, so any offset gap (compacted topics, transactional markers, or offsets filtered out upstream) permanently blocks commits for that partition. The `last_committed`, `all_offsets` and `outstanding` state is never cleared on rebalance, so stale state survives partition reassignment. Treat gaps as committable once all lower tracked offsets are complete, and clear per-partition state when partitions are revoked.

The commit scan assumes consecutive Kafka offsets and breaks at the first offset that is not in all_offsets. A permanent offset gap (compacted or transactional records) then blocks commits for that partition forever. Track the submitted offsets in sorted order and commit up to the highest offset below the lowest outstanding one, rather than requiring every integer in between to be present.

Determine the commit boundary from received offsets rather than requiring every integer in this range to exist. Kafka offsets need not be consecutive: if 100, 102 and 103 are delivered and completed, this scan stops at the nonexistent 101 even though there is no unfinished record. Conversely, after committing 100 and removing it, the next scan starts at 102 and commits past the gap, contradicting the added gap tests. Iterate received offsets in sorted order and stop at the first outstanding record; add a test covering legitimate skipped Kafka offsets across multiple commit cycles.

issues.descricao: OrderedQueueWorker marks a work item's offset complete in a finally block even when processing raised, so failed messages are committed and dropped, contradicting the documented guarantee of committing only after successful processing.

comentarios.texto: The worker marks the offset complete in the `finally` block even when `result_processor(...)` raises, so a message whose handling failed is reported as committable and its offset is committed (it will never be retried). This contradicts the strategy's own guarantee 'Only commits offsets after successful processing' and the new test `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling`, which asserts the partition is not committed after a failure. Only call `complete_offset` on the success path (or track failed offsets separately) so failures are not silently skipped.

The worker marks the offset complete in `finally` even when `result_processor` raised an exception, so a failed item's offset is reported as committable and gets committed by the commit loop. This contradicts the strategy's documented guarantee 'Only commits offsets after successful processing' and the contract asserted in test_results_consumer.py (test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling, which expects the failed partition NOT to be committed): the failed message is committed past and never retried. Track success separately and only call `complete_offset` when processing succeeded (or make the failure explicit so the offset is withheld/retried).

The failed item's offset is completed unconditionally in the `finally` block, so `complete_offset` runs even when `result_processor` raised. This breaks the class's documented guarantee ('Only commits offsets after successful processing', line 254): the commit loop then advances past a message that was never successfully processed, silently dropping it (and, per the PR's own test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling, a commit is produced where none is expected). Only call `offset_tracker.complete_offset(...)` on the success path (i.e. after `result_processor` returns normally), or explicitly decide and document the at-most-once semantics; do not complete on the exception path.

issues.descricao: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling's docstring says errors must not block commits for other messages, but the test asserts that nothing was committed, so it does not verify the behaviour it describes.
issues.textoGolden: The test test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling has a docstring that doesn't match the test implementation.

comentarios.texto: The commit assertion contradicts the test's own docstring and cannot fail for the reason it claims. The docstring says "errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages", but the body asserts `len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets` — i.e. it passes only when nothing is committed. In queue_consumer.py ordered worker's `finally` calls `complete_offset` even after result_processor raises (lines 148-149), so offset 100 should be committable and offset 101 should advance the commit; if the whole commit path were removed (commits blocked entirely) the test would still pass. Assert the positive behaviour instead: e.g. that the failing message's offset was still completed so commits progressed (expect `committed_offsets[test_partition] == 102`, matching the follow-on offset of the successfully processed message).

test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling claims errors don't block commits but asserts len(committed)==0 / not in, and waits only for total==0+sleep(0.2) while commit loop is 1.0s. It passes if commits are correctly made (checked before loop fires) and if commits are never made. Wait for commit condition and assert contiguous commit includes both offsets despite the exception.

issues.descricao: The error-handling test asserts no commit happened after only a 0.2s sleep while the commit loop runs every second, so it passes without ever observing whether a failed offset gets committed.

comentarios.texto: The error-handling test can pass even when failed messages are committed. It waits for two processor calls, sleeps only 0.2 seconds, and asserts that no commit has happened, whereas _commit_loop waits 1 second. OrderedQueueWorker currently completes the failed offset in finally, so the unsafe commit can occur after this assertion. Synchronize with an actual commit-loop iteration before asserting that it cannot advance past the failed offset.

issues.descricao: FixedQueuePool uses unbounded queues and the strategy never applies backpressure, so when workers fall behind the consumer keeps polling and queued work items grow memory without limit, contrary to the documented backpressure guarantee.

comentarios.texto: Each worker queue is created unbounded (queue.Queue() with no maxsize) although the class docstring promises 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up' and the strategy claims to guarantee backpressure. With no bound and no MessageRejected raised from submit(), a slow group continues to accumulate items in its queue while the consumer keeps polling, so memory grows without limit under a sustained backlog — the opposite of the intended protection. Fix: give the queues a maxsize and raise/return MessageRejected (or otherwise propagate backpressure to the caller) when a queue is full.

The `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` docstring promises "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but the queues this strategy drives are unbounded: `FixedQueuePool` creates each one as `queue.Queue()` with no maxsize (line 185), and `submit()` puts items unconditionally. Nothing ever blocks, so no backpressure exists. Either bound the queues (pass a `maxsize` and handle `queue.Full` / block in `submit`) or correct the docstring so it does not advertise a guarantee the code does not provide.

The pool creates unbounded queues, while strategy submit always accepts messages and poll never applies backpressure. When a queue's worker is slow or ingestion exceeds processing capacity, queued WorkItems retain both decoded results and original Kafka messages without any limit, causing growing memory consumption and eventual consumer OOM. Bound queued/in-flight work and raise Arroyo MessageRejected when capacity is reached, ensuring that rejection is not swallowed by the generic submit exception handler.

issues.descricao: Graceful shutdown sets each worker's shutdown flag before draining, so workers stop with items still queued, and close() stops the commit thread first, so finished work is not committed and gets replayed.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True while OrderedQueueWorker.run loops on while not self.shutdown, so workers exit without draining queued WorkItems even though queues are shut down with immediate=False. WHY: Graceful shutdown silently drops queued items and leaves their offsets in outstanding forever, causing reprocessing/duplicates and failing the claimed graceful-shutdown guarantee. HOW: Remove the shutdown-flag short-circuit and let workers drain until queue.ShutDown, e.g. loop unconditionally and break only on ShutDown.

close() stops the commit thread and shuts down workers before draining accepted work, and join() only repeats close() instead of waiting for processing and making a final commit. Pool shutdown sets worker.shutdown before workers can drain their queues, so assignment revocation abandons queued results and completed in-flight work is not finally committed, causing replay and allowing unfinished old work to overlap a new owner. Make close() stop acceptance without blocking, then have join() drain accepted work within its timeout and commit completed offsets before releasing workers.

Do not set worker.shutdown before draining the queues during graceful shutdown. If a worker is processing A while B is queued, shutdown sets the flag; after A finishes, the worker exits at `while not self.shutdown` without ever retrieving B. Calling queue.shutdown(immediate=False) does not override that loop condition. Drain accepted work before stopping workers, and keep committing available until that drain completes; currently close stops the commit thread before the workers as well, so even work finished during shutdown is not finally committed.

issues.descricao: The strategy's close() shuts down the factory-owned shared queue pool, so after a partition rebalance the next strategy reuses a dead pool; submissions fail and the error handler marks their offsets complete, committing messages that were never processed.

comentarios.texto: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() shuts down the FixedQueuePool, but that pool is a singleton owned by the factory (created once in ResultsStrategyFactory.__init__ and never recreated). Arroyo calls strategy.close() then join() on every assignment revocation/rebalance, and the factory's create_with_partitions is called again for the next assignment; the new strategy then reuses the already-shut-down queue_pool. Because q.shutdown(immediate=False) makes subsequent put() raise queue.ShutDown, submit()'s except branch (lines 317-325) swallows it and marks the offset complete, so after any rebalance every message is committed as processed without ever being handled — silent data loss. Fix: either let the factory own the pool lifecycle (don't shut it down from the strategy's close) and create a fresh pool per create_with_partitions, or reset/recreate factory.queue_pool when the strategy is closed.

WHAT: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close/terminate shuts down the factory-owned shared FixedQueuePool. WHY: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one queue_pool and hands it to every strategy from create_with_partitions, so Arroyo rebalance (close old strategy, create new one reusing factory.queue_pool) reuses a dead pool with joined workers and shut-down queues, stalling all further processing. HOW: Make pool lifecycle owned only by the factory: strategy close should only stop its commit thread, not call queue_pool.shutdown().

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close(), terminate() and join() shut down the FixedQueuePool, but that pool is created once by ResultsStrategyFactory and shared by every strategy it creates. After a rebalance, Arroyo closes the old strategy and then calls create_with_partitions again, which reuses the dead pool. Messages then fail to enqueue, and the submit() exception handler marks them complete, so their offsets get committed without the messages being processed. The strategy should only stop its own commit thread. The pool should be shut down only by factory.shutdown(), or the pool should be created per strategy.

issues.descricao: The strategy invokes Arroyo's commit callback from a background thread rather than from submit/poll on the consumer thread, so commits can race with polling and partition revocation on a non-thread-safe consumer.

comentarios.texto: `commit_function` is called from the background commit thread, but arroyo's commit callback is expected to be called from the main consumer thread, and the Kafka consumer is not thread-safe. Committing from another thread risks races with polling and with rebalances.

issues.descricao: The WorkItem docstring says the original message is kept for offset tracking, but offset tracking only uses partition and offset and the message field is never used.

comentarios.texto: The `WorkItem` docstring says it "includes the original message for offset tracking", but the `message` field is never used for offset tracking — `OffsetTracker` and the commit loop only ever read `partition`/`offset`, and `submit()` even re-derives the offset from `message.value` rather than from the stored `message`. Update the docstring to describe what the field is actually for (or remove the unused field) so it does not misdescribe the dataclass contract.

`WorkItem.message` is declared with the comment 'includes the original message for offset tracking' and is populated in `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit`, but nothing ever reads it — offset tracking uses the separate `partition`/`offset` fields. The declared purpose does not match any actual use, so the field (and the extra reference to each Kafka message it keeps alive) is dead; either use it for offset tracking or remove it.

issues.descricao: The tests named for concurrent processing across groups only check that all items were processed and all groups seen, so a fully serial implementation would pass and concurrency is never verified.

comentarios.texto: Test named/docstringed "Test that different groups are processed concurrently" never verifies concurrency. The body only asserts all 6 items ran and that three distinct group numbers were seen — a single worker draining one queue, or a fully serial FixedQueuePool, would satisfy both assertions. Either measure actual overlap (e.g. have result_processor block on a barrier/event until all three groups have entered, and fail on timeout) or drop the concurrency claim from the name/docstring.

test_thread_queue_parallel_concurrent_subscriptions claims to verify that different subscriptions are processed concurrently, but the only assertion is `mock_processor_call.call_count == 2`, which a strictly serial implementation also satisfies. Add a real concurrency signal (e.g. a barrier in the mocked processor that requires both calls to be in flight simultaneously before either returns), otherwise this test cannot detect loss of parallelism.

test_concurrent_processing_across_groups claims concurrent processing but only asserts 6 items processed and 3 groups seen. A serial/single-queue implementation would still pass. Verify overlap (blocking processor + timing/thread IDs) or remove concurrency claim.

issues.descricao: The strategy ordering test submits identical messages and only checks the count processed, so it cannot detect out-of-order processing within a group.

comentarios.texto: The strategy ordering test submits five identical decoded results for sub1 and only asserts their count. Processing them in reverse order would still pass. Give each message a distinguishable sequence value and assert the exact processed sequence, so this tests ordering through SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy rather than only delivery.

issues.descricao: The graceful-shutdown test only asserts that the factory cleared its queue_pool reference, which shutdown always does, so it does not verify that pending work is drained or workers stop.

comentarios.texto: This does not verify graceful shutdown: factory.shutdown unconditionally clears queue_pool after calling pool.shutdown, so the assertion passes even if pending messages are abandoned or worker threads remain alive. Retain the pool reference and assert that all submitted work completed and its workers stopped; the current worker shutdown flag can stop workers without draining their queues.

issues.descricao: The polling bound max_wait = 50 is repeated as a magic number across the thread-queue-parallel tests instead of a named constant.
issues.textoGolden: The magic number 50 for max_wait is used repeatedly throughout the tests. Consider extracting this as a named constant to improve maintainability.

issues.descricao: Claims queue.ShutDown and Queue.shutdown() are unavailable on Python < 3.13, so workers never exit on shutdown.

comentarios.texto: `queue.ShutDown` and `Queue.shutdown()` exist only in Python 3.13+, and the worker blocks forever on `get()` when shutdown is not available. On older Python versions, `except queue.ShutDown` raises AttributeError when evaluated, and `q.shutdown` fails in `FixedQueuePool.shutdown`, where the failure is swallowed. The worker threads then never exit. Use a sentinel item or a timeout on `get` for shutdown.

issues.descricao: Claims Python's randomized str hash makes group-to-queue assignment differ across processes, breaking per-subscription ordering and letting two processes handle the same subscription concurrently.

comentarios.texto: Queue selection uses the built-in `hash(group_key)`, which is randomized per process by PYTHONHASHSEED for str. Group-to-queue assignment therefore differs between consumer processes and after a restart. Ordering guarantees per subscription are lost across processes, and two processes can handle the same subscription concurrently. Use a stable hash such as `zlib.crc32(group_key.encode()) % num_queues` or md5.

issues.descricao: Claims FixedQueuePool.submit leaks an outstanding offset when put() raises after add_offset, permanently blocking commits for the partition.

comentarios.texto: FixedQueuePool.submit calls offset_tracker.add_offset before work_queue.put with no cleanup if put raises (e.g. after queue shutdown). The leaked outstanding offset can never complete and blocks later contiguous commits for that partition.

issues.descricao: Claims get_stats/wait_until_empty report empty while items are still in flight because qsize drops when a worker takes an item.

comentarios.texto: get_stats/wait_until_empty measures only sum(q.qsize()); qsize drops at get() before processing completes, so it reports empty/0 while items are in-flight. Include in-flight work (e.g. OffsetTracker outstanding) or unfinished_tasks before declaring empty.

issues.descricao: Claims metrics.incr receives len(committable) as the instance argument instead of the amount, so the commit count is always 1.

comentarios.texto: metrics.incr passes len(committable) as second positional arg (instance), not amount, so commit count is always 1 and instance is polluted with an int. Pass amount explicitly, e.g. amount=len(committable).

issues.descricao: The offsets_committed metric is incremented by the number of partitions being committed rather than the number of offsets, so its name misdescribes the value.

comentarios.texto: The metric `offsets_committed` is incremented by len(committable), which is the number of partitions committed, not the number of offsets. Emit the actual offset count (for example, the sum of newly committed offsets per partition), or rename the metric to partitions_committed.

issues.descricao: Claims factory shutdown leaves SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy commit threads running and committing after shutdown.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: ResultsStrategyFactory.shutdown shuts down queue_pool but never stops SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy commit threads created in the strategy constructor. WHY: The daemon commit loop keeps running after factory shutdown and keeps calling the stale commit_function/mark_committed, leaking threads and committing after shutdown/revoke. HOW: Track created strategies and call their close/terminate (or at least set shutdown_event and join commit_thread) from factory shutdown.

sugestoes.texto: The category lookup dereferences the first result before checking whether the query returned any rows. Sites without a stored embed_category setting, or whose configured category no longer exists, fail the migration before reaching the uncategorized fallback, even when embedding is unused. Read the first row safely and use the uncategorized category when no row is found.

The migration inserts legacy allowlist entries verbatim instead of stripping schemes and paths as EmbeddableHost's validation callback does. Existing entries such as http://discourse.org and https://example.com/1234 then never match record_for_host's bare URI hostname, disabling existing embeds and retrieval after upgrade. Normalize each migrated entry to the same stored representation as newly saved hosts before inserting it.

record_for_host compares URI.host with the stored host string, discarding the URL's port even though validation accepts host:port and normalization preserves it. An allowed entry such as example.com:8080 can be saved successfully but rejects every embedding request and retrieval for http://example.com:8080. Make storage and lookup use a consistent representation for explicitly configured ports.

The stored hostname is lowercased but the incoming URI hostname is not. Ruby URI preserves hostname case, although DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. Consequently an allowed host such as example.com is rejected when a referer or embed URL uses EXAMPLE.com, and the category lookup during import also fails for that equivalent identity. Normalize both operands before comparing.

When there is no stored embed_category setting (or its value no longer matches a category), this join returns no rows. Accessing [0]['id'] then raises on nil, aborting the migration before the category_id == 0 fallback can run. Check whether the result has a first row before accessing its id and use the uncategorized fallback for an empty result.

When embed_category has no stored row (for example an installation that never configured embedding), or its value does not match an existing category name, this join returns no rows. Indexing [0]['id'] then raises instead of reaching the uncategorized fallback. This aborts the entire migration even when there are no hosts to migrate. Read the first row defensively and handle the empty result before extracting its ID.

A create or update request with embeddable_host containing a null or omitted host assigns nil to host. This callback calls sub! on nil before the format validator executes, producing an unhandled exception rather than the controller's normal validation-error response. Guard the normalization for nil so the validator can reject the value.

The validator accepts entries such as `example.com:8080`, and before_validation preserves that port. However, URI#host returns only `example.com`, so this query can never find the saved `example.com:8080` record, even for `http://example.com:8080/page`. Both embed authorization and topic retrieval consequently reject this explicitly allowed host. Use a consistent port representation when saving and looking up hosts, while preserving existing portless-host semantics.

`lower(host)` is compared to the unchanged URI hostname. URI parsing preserves hostname case, so a request for `https://EXAMPLE.COM/page` fails to match a saved `example.com`, although DNS hostnames are case insensitive and the validator accepts either case. Normalize the incoming hostname as well so authorization and category lookup do not depend on URL capitalization.

The previous allowlist accepted full URLs (the existing controller test uses `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234`), but the new lookup compares `URI(url).host` directly with the stored host. This SQL copies those settings unchanged and bypasses the model callback that strips schemes and paths. After upgrading, those previously working hosts therefore fail authorization in both EmbedController and TopicRetriever. Normalize each migrated entry to the same bare-host representation as newly created records before inserting it.

Existing allowed hosts can contain full URLs (the changed embed controller specs show `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234` in the old setting). This inserts those values verbatim, bypassing the new model's normalization callback, but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` now compares only `URI(url).host` against the stored value. Consequently those hosts stop being allowed after upgrade, breaking existing embeds and retrieval. Normalize each migrated entry to its hostname before inserting it, consistently with the new lookup contract.

The removed outer setup used to enable embed_truncate and stub has_topic_embed? to true. This example now builds a topic with no embed, so expandable_first_post? is false regardless of whether an embeddable host is required. Indeed, the new implementation does not check hosts at all and this test still passes. Set the other predicates true and explicitly test the intended no-host behavior (or rename and restructure the example if host presence is intentionally no longer relevant), so this is not misleading coverage of the host condition.

issues.descricao: EmbeddableHost's before_validation calls self.host.sub! unconditionally, so saving a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error.
issues.textoGolden: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: The before_validation callback calls `sub!` on host without guarding nil. Creating a host with a missing or null host field reaches this callback from save_host and raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Guard nil during normalization and let presence/format validation reject it.

WHAT: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally, so a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError (`nil.sub!`) instead of producing a normal format-invalid result. WHY: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly; any request that omits the host value makes the save raise a 500 instead of returning the `render_json_error(host)` validation response. HOW: guard the mutation, e.g. `return if host.blank?` at the top of the before_validation block (or use `self.host = self.host.to_s` before stripping).

before_validation calls self.host.sub!(...) on a possibly-nil host before validates_format_of runs. The controller assigns host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host], so a request without a host key leaves it nil and nil.sub! raises NoMethodError at save time instead of the format validation producing a normal error response. Add a presence guard so validation reports the failure.

issues.descricao: update and destroy in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController fetch the host with where(id:).first and never check for nil, so an unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of not-found.
issues.textoGolden: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: In the destroy action, the nil-host case (line 15-16) would raise NoMethodError. Consider adding a nil check to handle the case where the host is not found.

update and destroy fetch the record with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first but never check for nil, then immediately use it (save_host(host) does host.host = ... / host.save; destroy does host.destroy). A stale or already-deleted id, or an interleaving where a concurrent delete removes the row first, makes host nil and the first call on it raises NoMethodError -> unhandled 500. Guard with a nil/404 check before use.

Update passes the nullable result of where(...).first directly to save_host, which immediately assigns host.host. Updating a nonexistent or concurrently deleted record returns an internal error instead of a not-found response; destroy has the same lookup failure. Use find or explicitly raise a not-found error before dereferencing the lookup result.

issues.descricao: record_for_host compares lower(host) against the un-lowercased URI host, so mixed-case referer hosts fail to match allowed hosts and embedding is rejected.
issues.textoGolden: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

comentarios.texto: Normalize the parsed hostname before comparing it with lower(host). URI parsing preserves hostname case, so an allowed entry such as example.com does not match https://EXAMPLE.com/page even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. This makes valid embedding requests fail the host authorization check and makes category lookup inconsistent for equivalent domain identities. Compare against host.downcase (or normalize both operands equivalently), and add a mixed-case URL test.

The query compares lower(host) to the un-downcased uri.host. A referer such as http://EvilTrout.com never matches the stored lowercase host, so embedding is wrongly denied. Fix: use where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase).

The query compares lower(host) in the database with uri.host, which is not lowercased, so the comparison normalizes only one side. A referer or URL with uppercase letters (e.g. http://EvilTrout.com) will not match the stored host. Compare against host.downcase, i.e. where('lower(host) = ?', host.downcase).

issues.descricao: The migration copies the legacy embeddable_hosts values into the new table without stripping scheme and path, so hosts stored as http://example.com no longer match the bare-host lookup and previously allowed embeds are rejected after upgrade.
issues.textoGolden: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration inserts raw embeddable_hosts lines (e.g. http://example.com/123) without stripping scheme/path like the model does. WHY: migrated rows never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host which compares bare uri.host, silently breaking previously allowed embeds.

Migration INSERTs raw embeddable_hosts lines with scheme/path intact, but EmbeddableHost normalizes to bare domain (before_validation strips protocol/path, record_for_host looks up by URI.host). Strip protocol and path before INSERT or migrated hosts will never satisfy host_allowed?.

Legacy hosts are inserted verbatim instead of applying the new model's scheme/path normalization. Existing values such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 remain in the table, while record_for_host compares only URI.host, so previously configured embedding hosts stop working after upgrade. Normalize migrated entries to the same representation used by the model before inserting them.

issues.descricao: The contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped, so each file defines the other's fabricators.
issues.textoGolden: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

comentarios.texto: File named category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while Fabricator(:category) was moved to embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Filenames disagree with contents — swap contents back so each file defines the fabricator its name states.

The file names and contents are swapped. embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category), and category_fabricator.rb defines :embeddable_host. Restore category_fabricator.rb to the original category fabricators and put the :embeddable_host fabricator in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

issues.descricao: The migration builds its INSERT by interpolating each legacy host value into the SQL string instead of quoting or binding it, so a value with a quote breaks the statement.
issues.textoGolden: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

comentarios.texto: The migration's INSERT statement uses string interpolation: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). This is a SQL-injection concern and should be fixed by using parameterized queries or proper escaping.
WHAT: migration interpolates raw host string into SQL: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). WHY: a host value containing a single quote breaks the statement and allows SQL injection via site_settings value.

issues.descricao: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.
issues.textoGolden: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] with no guard when embed_category setting/category is missing. WHY: nil[0] dereference crashes the migration and blocks deploy on instances without that setting.
Migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking empty result; missing site_settings row throws NoMethodError and fails migration. Check for nil row.

The migration indexes the first category-query result before checking whether any row was returned. An installation without a persisted embed_category setting, or with no matching category name, aborts migration before reaching the uncategorized fallback. Check whether the result contains a row before accessing its id and handle missing fallback settings as well.

issues.descricao: The spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer sets up any host condition and passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false, so its name no longer matches what it tests.

comentarios.texto: Test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' does not establish the true-branch preconditions (embed_truncate true, has_topic_embed true) nor control host presence, so it passes regardless of host logic and would still pass if host checking were broken/removed. Set truncate true + stub embed true with no hosts for the false case.

The test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now uses an ordinary built topic without setting embed_truncate or making has_topic_embed? true. It therefore returns false for reasons unrelated to the missing host, and passes even with the new implementation that never checks host availability. If blank-host behavior remains the intended contract, arrange all the other prerequisites before asserting false; if the contract intentionally changed, replace this case with a test of the actual intended behavior rather than retaining a misleading passing test.

The description "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer matches the code. This PR changed Topic#expandable_first_post? (app/models/topic.rb:869) to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing the embeddable_hosts condition entirely, and removed the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` setup from this test. The assertion now passes only because `has_topic_embed?` is unstubbed (false) and embed_truncate is unset, so the name states a cause the method no longer has — rename it (e.g. "is false when there is no topic embed") or set up the precondition it claims to test.

issues.descricao: The 'find embedded' test requests fruit 2 but the pretender always returns fruit 1, so it asserts fruit 1's colors and would not notice a find that ignores the id.

comentarios.texto: Test requests fruit id 2 but pretender returns fruits[0] unconditionally, so assertions on colors [1,2] never cover fruit 2's color_ids [3]. Make pretender honor :id or request id 1 / assert single-element case to actually verify plural _ids hydration.

This test now requests fruit 2 but expects fruit 1's two colors. The /fruits/:id Pretender handler always returns fruits[0], so the test passes while hydrating the wrong record and would not catch a find implementation that ignores the requested ID. Make the handler select the requested fruit and assert its ID and corresponding colors (fruit 2 has only color 3), or request fruit 1 if testing its two-color hydration is the goal.

issues.descricao: After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.

comentarios.texto: The save callback overwrites the category using categoryId even when the server substituted the uncategorized category for a blank selection. Adding a host without choosing a category therefore leaves its category badge empty, and editing it reads an undefined category id despite a valid category_id having been returned. Resolve the category from the saved response's category_id rather than the submitted selection.

When categoryId is null (the default for a new row, or a cleared selection), the controller saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that category_id. This callback instead overwrites host.category with findById(null), making the displayed category disagree with the saved category. Use the category from the save response or its returned category_id rather than the pre-save selection.

Use the saved response's category rather than overwriting it from categoryId after saving. For a new host with no category selected, categoryId is null, while the new controller deliberately saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that ID through the serializer. This callback replaces the hydrated category with findById(null), leaving the row without its actual category until reload (and reopening edit also initializes from that incorrect relationship).

issues.descricao: Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.

comentarios.texto: Host lookup compares URI.host against a stored value that validation explicitly permits to include a port. Saving example.com:8080 succeeds, but a request from http://example.com:8080 produces URI.host equal to example.com and never matches that record, disabling embedding and retrieval for the configured host. Use a consistent port representation in both storage and lookup.

The validator accepts hosts such as `example.com:8080`, but record_for_host extracts only URI.host (`example.com`) and compares it to the stored port-qualified string. An accepted and saved host therefore never authorizes its corresponding URLs. Normalize the stored and queried authority consistently, including a deliberate port policy.

issues.descricao: Claims expandable_first_post? lost its 'embeddable hosts configured' guard and now expands first posts when no EmbeddableHost exists.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `expandable_first_post?` dropped the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard and now returns true whenever `embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?` are true, with no check that any embeddable host is actually configured. WHY: a topic whose embed was created by a host that has since been deleted still gets its first post expanded, changing embed output for a state the previous guard blocked; the retained "is false if embeddable_host is blank" spec no longer exercises host presence (has_topic_embed? is unstubbed/false), so this regression is not caught. HOW: gate on the new source of truth, e.g. `EmbeddableHost.exists? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` if host presence is still required.

expandable_first_post? used to return false when no embeddable hosts were configured. The new version drops that guard (`SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?`) and does not replace it with `EmbeddableHost.exists?`. A forum with no embeddable hosts but with embed_truncate on and a topic embed now gets an expandable first post. Restore the guard by checking `EmbeddableHost.exists?`.

WHAT: expandable_first_post? dropped the hosts-present guard and now returns true for any embedded topic even with zero EmbeddableHost rows. WHY: UI offers expand on first post when embedding is effectively unconfigured, a regression from SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? check.

issues.descricao: Claims the plural *_ids hydration branch crashes on non-array values and keeps undefined entries for missing ids.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: plural branch calls obj[k].map without checking it is an array and keeps undefined entries for missing ids. WHY: null/non-array *_ids payload or dangling id crashes hydration or yields array with undefined models instead of filtering/fallback.

issues.descricao: Claims Admin::EmbeddingController#update persists nothing, so the client's saveChanges appears to succeed without saving.

comentarios.texto: The update action does not change or persist anything and only re-renders the embedding. The client's saveChanges therefore appears to succeed while doing nothing.

issues.descricao: Claims EmbeddingSerializer emits only embeddable_host_ids without sideloading the host records, so the admin host table renders empty.

comentarios.texto: `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids` emits only `embeddable_host_ids` in the show/update response and never sideloads the EmbeddableHost records. The admin client, however, consumes `embedding.embeddable_hosts` as full objects (store.js `_hydrateEmbedded` looks each id up via `_lookupSubType` and assigns the resolved records; `embedding.hbs` iterates them and `embeddable-host.hbs` reads `host.host`/`host.category`). With ids-only and no concurrent sideload, `_lookupSubType` resolves nothing, so the host table renders empty on first load of /admin/customize/embedding. Embed the objects (e.g. `embed: :ids, include: true`, or `embed: :objects`) so the payload carries the `embeddable_hosts` records the client now requires.

`has_many :embeddable_hosts, ..., embed: :ids` without `include: true` emits only `embeddable_host_ids` and never sideloads the embedded objects, but the consumer `store._hydrateEmbedded` resolves those ids through `_lookupSubType`, which reads `root['embeddable_hosts']`. With the collection absent every id hydrates to `undefined`, so the admin embedding page shows no/blank hosts. Add `include: true` so the collection the store requires is actually serialized.

sugestoes.texto: The team authorization predicate requires both admin and owner status. isTeamAdmin accepts ADMIN or OWNER, but isTeamOwner accepts only OWNER, so team admins who are neither organizer nor attendee receive FORBIDDEN. Use isTeamAdmin alone, which already includes owners.

The blacklist comparison uses unnormalized guest input against lowercased blacklist entries. An authorized caller can supply a mixed-case version of a blocked address and cause an invitation to that blocked mailbox. Normalize the guest address before comparing it with the blacklist.

uniqueGuests filters against existing attendees but does not deduplicate the submitted guests array. Direct mutation calls containing the same new email twice insert duplicate Attendee records and send duplicate invitations, because the server schema accepts duplicates and Attendee has no uniqueness constraint. Deduplicate the submitted array before filtering.

The reconstructed CalendarEvent omits the booking's persisted iCalUID. generateIcsString consequently uses booking.uid for the new REQUEST attachments, so bookings whose stored iCalUID differs receive invitations with a different identity rather than updates to the original calendar event. Carry booking.iCalUID into the event passed to the calendar updater and email sender.

The uniqueness check exists only in the dialog. The server schema accepts, for example, guests: ["new@example.com", "new@example.com"], and both entries pass this filter when that address is not already an attendee. Both are then passed to createMany, resulting in duplicate attendee records (or a failed mutation if a database constraint rejects them). Enforce uniqueness server-side before constructing guestsFullDetails; client-side validation does not protect this mutation from direct API requests.

Blacklist entries are lowercased above, but `guest` retains the caller's casing: neither the input schema's `.email()` nor the UI normalizes it. With `blocked@example.com` configured, submitting `Blocked@example.com` passes this filter and adds and sends an invitation to the blocked mailbox. Normalize the guest address before the blacklist comparison so casing cannot bypass the restriction.

The removal tooltip is hard-coded in English, so users viewing the new guest dialog in another locale still see “Remove email,” even though the surrounding controls use `t`. Route this tooltip through the translation mechanism and provide its translation key.

The variable named uniqueGuests is not actually unique: the filter only checks attendees already stored on the booking. A request with guests: ["new@example.com", "new@example.com"] passes the server schema and retains both entries, which are then passed to createMany and produce duplicate attendees (or a database failure if uniqueness is enforced). The dialog's refinement does not protect direct API calls. Deduplicate the submitted list before filtering and persisting it.

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is explicitly lowercased when read, but guest is compared in its original casing. Consequently a valid mixed-case address such as Blocked@example.com passes even when blocked@example.com is configured, and is persisted and sent an invitation. Normalize the candidate for the blacklist comparison as well.

issues.descricao: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.
issues.textoGolden: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && instead of ||. WHY: isTeamAdmin returns truthy for role ADMIN or OWNER while isTeamOwner returns true only for OWNER, so the && expression is only true for OWNERs; team ADMINs are treated as unauthorized and get FORBIDDEN when adding guests, contradicting the variable's intent. HOW: use `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) || (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`.

The flag is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` but is computed with `&&` (both admin AND owner). A team admin who is not the owner, or the owner who is not flagged admin, will fail this check, so the guard at line 54 wrongly throws FORBIDDEN for legitimate admins/owners. Use `||` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner.

The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` names an OR condition, but the code combines `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)` with `&&`, so it is true only when the user is both admin AND owner. Either the name is wrong or the operator is; as written the permission check at line 54 denies a plain team admin, contradicting what the identifier promises. Use `||` to match the name (or rename if AND is intended).

issues.descricao: The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
issues.textoGolden: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The blacklist is compared case-sensitively against guest input while blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased. WHY: blacklistedGuestEmails entries are lowercased but the filter compares `guest` verbatim (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`); an authenticated user can add a blacklisted address simply by changing its case (e.g. `Foo@bar.com` vs `foo@bar.com`), bypassing the configured BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restriction. HOW: normalize the guest before comparison, e.g. `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())`.

Case-sensitivity bypass of the guest blacklist. `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased on the list side (line 71) but the input side is compared raw: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` (line 77). A guest email submitted with any different casing (e.g. `Foo@Bar.com` when the blacklist holds `foo@bar.com`) passes the filter and is persisted, defeating BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS. Normalize the input before comparison, e.g. filter on `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())` (and likewise lowercase `guest` for the attendee dedup check).

WHAT: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but the incoming guest string is compared without lowercasing/normalizing. WHY: an attacker bypasses the blocklist with case variation (e.g. Spam@Example.com) and gets added/emailed.

issues.descricao: The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.
issues.textoGolden: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: uniqueGuests filter only dedupes against existing booking.attendees with case-sensitive === and never dedupes duplicates within the input guests array itself (server schema has no uniqueness refine unlike the client). WHY: a request with the same new email twice creates duplicate attendee rows via createMany.

uniqueGuests filters only against existing attendees/blacklist but never dedupes guests[] itself and schema has no uniqueness check. A request like guests=[a@x.com,a@x.com] passes the filter twice and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows or throws an unhandled DB unique-constraint exception. Dedupe/normalize input (and reject intra-request duplicates) before createMany.

uniqueGuests filters against existing attendees but does not deduplicate addresses within the incoming guests array. A direct mutation with the same new address twice inserts two Attendee records and sends duplicate invitations because the server schema permits duplicates and the Attendee model has no unique booking/email constraint. Deduplicate normalized input before filtering and inserting.

issues.descricao: Check-then-insert without a transaction or unique constraint lets two concurrent addGuests calls for the same email both pass the existing-attendee check and create duplicate attendees.

comentarios.texto: Race condition: findFirst check for existing attendees then booking.update+createMany is not atomic. Two concurrent addGuests calls with the same new email both see it as absent and both insert, creating duplicates. Guard with a unique constraint and handle conflict or run in a transaction/serializable check.

Check-then-insert race: the handler reads `booking.attendees` at the start, filters against it, then inserts in a separate `prisma.booking.update ... createMany` with no transaction or unique guard. Two concurrent addGuests calls for the same guest both see it as absent and both insert, producing duplicate attendees. Wrap the read+filter+insert in a transaction (or rely on a unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and handle the conflict) so concurrent requests cannot both succeed.

issues.descricao: Attendee authorization and existing-attendee dedup compare emails case-sensitively, so an attendee with differently-cased stored email is FORBIDDEN and a case-variant of an existing attendee is added again.

comentarios.texto: Inconsistent email normalization for identity checks. Both the authorization check `attendee.email === user.email` (line 52) and the existing-attendee dedup `guest === attendee.email` (line 76) use strict case-sensitive equality, while emails are treated as case-insensitive everywhere else in this handler (the blacklist block directly below lowercases). Consequence: a legitimate attendee whose stored casing differs from their session email is wrongly FORBIDDEN, and a guest differing from an existing attendee only by case is duplicated rather than filtered. Compare on a normalized form (both sides `.toLowerCase()`), consistent with the blacklist normalization.

issues.descricao: The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.
issues.textoGolden: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the raw input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests. WHY: already-existing attendees included in the request are misclassified as newGuests in email-manager and receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (wrong notification).

Dead-transform / wrong input: `uniqueGuests` is computed (dedup vs existing attendees + blacklist) and written to DB, but `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original `guests`. Existing attendees re-submitted are then `includes()`-matched as new and get AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

Pass `uniqueGuests` (the filtered set written to DB) to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of raw `guests`; the email layer assumes newGuests exactly equals newly created attendees for its Scheduled vs AddGuests branch.

issues.descricao: EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.

comentarios.texto: EventManager is initialized with the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's credentials. When an attendee or team owner adds guests to a booking whose calendar reference lacks credentialId, updateAllCalendarEvents selects credentials by type from the caller's calendars, so the organizer's event is not updated or the update targets the wrong account. Load credentials for booking.userId and initialize the manager with the booking owner.

issues.descricao: Claims a failing calendar update at addGuests.handler.ts:165 aborts the mutation after guests are persisted; the calendar update path already swallows provider errors.

comentarios.texto: The attendees are written to the database at line 92, but `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` at line 165 runs outside the try/catch. If it throws, the mutation returns an error even though the guests are already persisted, so the DB and the calendar are out of sync. No emails are sent, and a retry then fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. Catch and handle the calendar update failure after the DB write.

The attendees are already committed to the DB when `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited without a try/catch. If the calendar sync throws, the mutation returns an error and skips the emails, although the guests were added. The caller sees a failure for a partly applied change and may retry. Handle calendar sync failure as best-effort, as the email send is, or run it before the DB write.

issues.descricao: Claims any attendee can add guests and trigger invites; this is the deliberate permission model of the new feature.

comentarios.texto: Any attendee, matched only by email, is allowed to add arbitrary guests to a booking, and the handler then sends emails and calendar invites on the organizer's behalf. Any attendee can use this to send invites to arbitrary addresses. Restrict the action to the organizer and team admins, or verify that the attendee's email is confirmed.

issues.descricao: The guests array has no server-side size limit, so any authorized caller, including an attendee, can add thousands of guests and trigger an unbounded batch of inserts and emails.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: guests is an unbounded z.array(z.string().email()) with no max length. WHY: any authorized caller (including a mere attendee) can submit thousands of emails causing unbounded createMany inserts plus unbounded Promise.all email fanout in sendAddGuestsEmails.

The mutation accepts an unbounded guest array that is persisted and immediately expanded into concurrent emails to every attendee. For non-seated bookings each email's ICS serializes the full attendee list, so adding N guests creates O(N) concurrent sends and O(N²) aggregate attachment work; repeated additions also resend to all existing attendees. Enforce a server-side guest-count and total-attendee limit before insertion and bound notification concurrency.

issues.descricao: The Remove email tooltip in MultiEmail is a hard-coded English string instead of a translation key.

comentarios.texto: Tooltip content="Remove email" is hard-coded English user-facing text bypassing i18n while surrounding strings in the same file/PR use t(). Wrap it in t() e.g. content={t("remove_email")} and add the key to locales.

`Tooltip content="Remove email"` is a hard-coded English user-facing string, while the surrounding code in this same component routes user text through `t()` (e.g. `t("add_another")` on line 69). This string bypasses the translation mechanism and will never be localised; it should use a translation key.

The new removal tooltip hard-codes `Remove email`, so users in non-English locales see English text even though the neighbouring controls use `t(...)` and this component already obtains `t` from useLocale. Route this tooltip through a translation key (and supply its English translation) rather than using the literal.

issues.descricao: The onError fallback to unable_to_add_guests is unreachable because the template-string message is always truthy.

comentarios.texto: Unreachable fallback: `message` is a template string `${code}: ${...}` which is always truthy, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never takes the fallback. Build message conditionally or test the underlying parts for emptiness.

In `onError`, `message` is always a non-empty template string (`"${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}"`), so the fallback `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` is unreachable and the newly added `unable_to_add_guests` translation is never shown. The user is instead shown a raw error code prefix like `BAD_REQUEST: ...` rather than the translated message; the fallback and code prefix handling should be corrected so the intended translated text reaches the user.

The error message is built as a template string, so it is always truthy. The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is therefore dead code, and the user can see "undefined: ..." or an untranslated raw message. Use `err.message ? t(err.message) : t("unable_to_add_guests")`.

issues.descricao: After a validation failure followed by a successful add, isInvalidEmail stays true, so the stale emails_must_be_unique_valid error shows the next time the dialog is opened.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: addGuestsMutation onSuccess resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog but never resets isInvalidEmail. WHY: after one failed validation the red emails_must_be_unique_valid error persists on the next open/successful add.

issues.descricao: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.
issues.textoGolden: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

issues.descricao: Claims newGuests.includes(attendee.email) misroutes newly added guests whose casing differs from the stored value, but new attendees are stored with exactly the submitted string.

comentarios.texto: Case-sensitive identity comparison misroutes emails. `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` compares the freshly-added guest list against stored attendee emails with strict case-sensitive matching. A newly added guest whose casing differs from the stored value falls into the `else` branch and receives the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail template intended for pre-existing attendees, while existing attendees can receive the wrong one. Normalize both sides (e.g. compare `attendee.email.toLowerCase()` against a lowercased newGuests set).

issues.descricao: Suggests starting with [] instead of [""] because the empty string may cause validation issues; the empty initial field is intentional and validated.
issues.textoGolden: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

sugestoes.texto: The new backup-code branch accepts a valid backupCode even when a supplied totpCode is invalid, but the preceding password check is skipped whenever totpCode is nonempty. A caller can submit a valid backup code and totpCode="x" to authenticate to a password-based account without knowing its password. Require password verification for backup-code authentication regardless of whether totpCode was also supplied.

Backup-code consumption overwrites the encrypted list from the earlier user snapshot using only the user ID as its update condition. Concurrent logins can both authenticate using the same one-time code; logins consuming different codes can also overwrite each other's changes and restore a consumed code. Atomically compare the stored ciphertext against user.backupCodes when updating and reject or retry authentication if the conditional update affects no row.

Backup-code consumption writes a modified copy of the codes read earlier without checking whether that stored value has changed. Two concurrent requests using the same code can both pass verification and both authenticate. Requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's removal, leaving a previously used code valid again. This contradicts the exactly-once behavior described by backup_code_instructions. Consume with a conditional update against the original encrypted backupCodes value and reject/retry if no row was updated, or serialize verification and consumption with appropriate database locking.

The new backup-code authentication path uses Array.indexOf to compare an attacker-supplied credential against decrypted secrets. String equality and the early-exiting array search are not constant-time, exposing a timing oracle during second-factor verification. The same comparison is introduced in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61. Use a shared constant-time verification routine in both endpoints: validate the normalized code's fixed format, compare equal-length buffers with crypto.timingSafeEqual, and scan every stored slot without exiting on a match (handling consumed null entries with fixed-length dummy buffers).

The success toast is shown unconditionally after starting writeText in EnableTwoFactorModal. Removing the clipboard write entirely, or copying the wrong text, still passes this check. Read the clipboard after clicking (with the appropriate browser permissions) and compare it with the displayed backup codes so the test verifies the copy effect rather than only its notification.

The filename comes from the anchor's fixed download attribute, independently of the Blob contents. If backup-code serialization produces empty or incorrect text, this test still passes even though the downloaded recovery codes are unusable. Read the downloaded file and compare its contents to the displayed backup codes in addition to checking its filename.

Backup-code consumption is a read-modify-write without a concurrency check. Two requests can read the same stored array and both validate the same code before either update, so both logins succeed despite the exactly-once guarantee. If they use different codes, the last update also restores the code consumed by the first request. Make consumption atomic, for example by conditionally updating where both the user ID and original encrypted backupCodes match, and only accepting the login if exactly one row was updated (retry validation on a conflict).

issues.descricao: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

comentarios.texto: The new backup-code branch authenticates without guaranteeing the password check ran: password verification at line 121 is gated on `!credentials.totpCode`, and the branch at line 131 triggers on any truthy `credentials.backupCode` regardless of that gate. A POST to the credentials callback supplying a valid backup code together with any non-empty totpCode therefore takes the backup branch (skipping TOTP validation) while line 121 skips password verification — granting a session using only a second-factor backup code, with no account password. Require the password check before the backup branch, or include backupCode in the guard at line 121 (e.g. `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode && !credentials.backupCode)`).

The backup-code branch accepts a valid backup code even when an arbitrary nonempty totpCode has skipped password verification. The preceding guards at lines 113–125 trust the presence of totpCode, but this new branch does not validate it, allowing a holder of a backup code to log in to a password account without knowing its password by submitting both fields. Require password verification for backup-code authentication rather than allowing an unverified totpCode to bypass it.

WHAT: The new backup-code login branch authenticates without verifying the password when credentials also contain any totpCode value (password check at line 121 is skipped when totpCode is truthy, and the backup branch never checks it). WHY: An attacker holding only a backup code can add a dummy totpCode to the credentials callback and log in without the password, reducing two factors to one. HOW: Verify the password whenever backupCode is used (or decouple the password check from totpCode presence).

issues.descricao: After enabling 2FA, onEnable is only called from the backup-codes Close button; dismissing the dialog by Escape/overlay never notifies the parent, so the settings page keeps showing 2FA disabled.

comentarios.texto: On a successful enable (response.status === 200) the modal no longer calls onEnable(); it only advances to SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes, and onEnable() is now invoked solely from the 'close' button (line 269). If the user dismisses the Dialog via ESC or an overlay click, DialogContent's onOpenChange fires (wired to a plain setEnableModalOpen toggle at apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64 and the conditional render at apps/web/components/security/TwoFactorAuthSection.tsx:36), so onEnable never runs. The parent callbacks (setEnableModalOpen(false) + utils.viewer.me.invalidate() / setEnabled(true)) are skipped, leaving the 2FA Switch unchecked and the UI showing 2FA as disabled even though the server has enabled it. Call onEnable() from the dismiss path (onOpenChange) or when transitioning into DisplayBackupCodes, not only from the Close button.

Successful enablement no longer invokes onEnable until the backup-code screen's explicit Close button is clicked. Dismissing that screen through the dialog's onOpenChange instead only closes it in the parent and does not invalidate viewer.me, leaving the settings switch showing disabled even though the server has enabled 2FA. Ensure dismissal after successful enablement also invokes the completion callback and resets the setup state.

After a successful enable, `onEnable()` is no longer called and is only called from the backup-codes Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog by Escape or overlay click (`onOpenChange`) while the codes are displayed, the parent is never notified that 2FA is enabled. The modal also keeps its step state and the plaintext backup codes. Call `onEnable` when 2FA is enabled, or make the dialog's `onOpenChange(false)` on the DisplayBackupCodes step run the same handler as Close, which resets state and clears `backupCodes`.

issues.descricao: The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named TwoFactor, a copy-paste leftover from the TOTP component.
issues.textoGolden: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
