The copied identifier misstates what the component is; rename the function to `BackupCode` so the name matches the file, the imports and the rendered content.

The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`, which is the name of the separate TOTP component. It is a copy-paste leftover and misleads readers and stack traces. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

Component in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor` (`export default function TwoFactor`) while the file is BackupCode.tsx and it is imported as `BackupCode`. The name disagrees with the code's contract and duplicates the real TwoFactor component, misleading callers/readers. Rename to `BackupCode`.

issues.descricao: The backup-code copy e2e test only waits for the success toast, which is shown unconditionally, so it never verifies the clipboard content.

comentarios.texto: This 'copy' test does not verify the copy behaviour it names: it clicks backup-codes-copy and then only waits for the toast-success element. The handler (EnableTwoFactorModal) runs navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) without awaiting it and then calls showToast(...) unconditionally, so the toast appears even when the clipboard write is removed or fails. The assertion therefore passes with the backup-code copy feature broken; assert the actual effect (clipboard content, or that the formatted codes reached writeText) instead of the toast.

The copy test only waits for a success toast, but the implementation emits that toast unconditionally without awaiting navigator.clipboard.writeText. Removing the clipboard write entirely, copying an empty string, or rejecting the write would still pass this test. Read the clipboard after the click and compare its contents with the displayed backup codes so the test verifies the actual copy effect.
Copy test only waits for toast-success, explicitly TODOing clipboard check. Broken writeText (wrong format/empty) still passes; assert clipboard content equals formatted backup codes.

issues.descricao: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent logins can accept the same backup code more than once or overwrite each other's removal.
issues.textoGolden: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

comentarios.texto: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: the code is validated with indexOf (line 144) and only then persisted via prisma.user.update (line 149), with no unique constraint or lock. Two concurrent login requests sending the same valid backup code both read the unchanged row, both pass the indexOf check, and both obtain a session, violating the 'each backup code can be used exactly once' invariant. Consume the code atomically (e.g. a conditional update on the raw encrypted value / a dedicated used-backup-codes table with a unique index) so only one request can succeed.

Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, breaking the stated invariant that each backup code is single-use. Two concurrent login requests with the same backup code both read the same user.backupCodes array and both pass `index !== -1` before either `prisma.user.update` commits; both then persist a stale array (each nulling only its own index), so the code authenticates twice. Make consumption atomic (e.g. compare-and-swap on the encrypted value/updatedAt, a transaction with a conditional update, or an optimistic-locking retry) so exactly one request can claim a given code.

Backup-code consumption overwrites the encrypted list by user ID without checking that the stored list still matches the value read before verification. Concurrent requests can both authenticate with the same single-use code, and requests using different codes can overwrite each other's removals and restore a consumed code. Use a conditional atomic update matching the original backupCodes ciphertext and reject or retry authentication if no row was updated.

issues.descricao: The copy button shows a success toast without awaiting clipboard.writeText, so a failed copy still tells the user their backup codes were saved.

comentarios.texto: The handler shows “Backup codes copied!” immediately after calling `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, without awaiting its promise. If clipboard access is denied or the write otherwise rejects, the user still receives a success message and may close the dialog believing their recovery codes were saved. Await the clipboard write and show the success toast only after it resolves; handle rejection with an appropriate translated failure message.

issues.descricao: The download e2e test checks only the filename, not that the file contains the displayed backup codes.

comentarios.texto: The download assertion checks only the static filename from the anchor's download attribute. It still passes if the blob contains empty or incorrect backup codes, leaving the essential recovery-code export behavior unverified. Read the downloaded file and compare its contents to the displayed codes, including their formatting.

Download test only asserts suggestedFilename, explicitly TODOing file-content check. Empty/wrong backupCodes blob with correct filename still passes; assert downloaded file lines equal displayed/formatted backup codes.

issues.descricao: The disable endpoint's error log says 'backup code login' although it is disabling 2FA.
issues.textoGolden: Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

comentarios.texto: The error log says "cannot proceed with backup code login", but this endpoint disables two-factor authentication and does not log in. Change the message to describe disabling 2FA with a backup code.

issues.descricao: resetState does not clear backup codes/secret or revoke the backup-codes object URL, leaving a small blob URL leaked per setup cycle.
issues.textoGolden: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: resetState() clears only password/error/step and never clears backupCodes, secret, dataUri, nor revokes backupCodesUrl. WHY: Closing the modal after setup leaves TOTP secret and backup codes in memory and leaks the Blob object URL on every setup/close cycle. HOW: Clear those states and call URL.revokeObjectURL in resetState and on unmount.

issues.descricao: The disable endpoint calls replaceAll on req.body.backupCode without checking it is a string, so non-string input throws a 500.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll assumes a string with no type guard. WHY: A non-string JSON value (number/array) throws TypeError and returns 500 instead of the 400 IncorrectBackupCode contract, breaking error handling and enabling error-probing. HOW: Validate typeof backupCode === 'string' (or String(...)) before replaceAll.

issues.descricao: Backup codes are matched case-sensitively against lowercase hex, so a user typing the code in uppercase is rejected.
issues.textoGolden: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

issues.descricao: Claims a caller of the changed TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable still passes two arguments, but that caller uses a different, unchanged API module.

comentarios.texto: TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable gained a required third parameter `backupCode`, but not every caller was updated. apps/web/components/security/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:38 still calls `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable(password, totpCode)` with only two arguments. This is now a type error (missing required argument) and sends `backupCode: undefined` at runtime. Update that consumer to pass the backup code (or make the parameter optional) so the signature change is followed through everywhere it is used.

issues.descricao: The enable-2FA test asserts toBeTruthy on the un-awaited isChecked() Promise, so it passes regardless of the switch state, including now that the backup-codes step is never dismissed.

comentarios.texto: This assertion cannot fail: page.locator(...).isChecked() returns a Promise<boolean>, and expect(promise).toBeTruthy() is true for any Promise, so it passes whether the switch is checked or not (the PR's own FIXME notes this). Use `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()` so the check actually reflects the switch state.

Assertion `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` never fails: isChecked() returns a Promise which is always truthy. Must be `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()` or `expect(await locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()`. First enable-2FA test therefore passes even after PR inserts DisplayBackupCodes step it never dismisses.

issues.descricao: Backup codes are compared with indexOf/=== instead of a constant-time comparison, theoretically leaking timing information.

comentarios.texto: The submitted backup code is matched against stored codes with `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, i.e. ordinary short-circuiting string equality on an authentication credential. String comparison returns early on the first differing byte, so response timing can leak how much of a code the attacker guessed. Compare with a constant-time comparison (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual` over equal-length buffers) instead of `indexOf`/`===`.

The disable endpoint validates the backup code with `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, a non-constant-time string comparison of a security credential, leaking correctness via execution time. Use a constant-time comparison (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers) rather than `indexOf`/`===`.

Backup codes are authentication secrets, but indexOf compares their plaintext strings using ordinary equality and stops at the first match. This is not a constant-time credential check and can expose comparison-dependent timing. Validate the normalized code's format/length, compare fixed-length buffers with crypto.timingSafeEqual, and scan all stored slots without early termination (including handling consumed null slots) before deciding whether authentication succeeds.

issues.descricao: Suggests a clearer post-2FA redirect journey in a file that does not exist.

comentarios.texto: After two-factor authentication completes, consider implementing a clear user journey: either redirect to a dedicated two-factor page or conditionally render the two-factor component based on user state.

comentarios.texto: Add error handling to clear the polling interval when a 2FA attempt fails, and ensure the interval is cleared on component unmount to avoid memory leaks.

issues.descricao: Reports no issue.

comentarios.texto: No defect of the assigned class found: every truthiness test is on a value whose only falsy state is the intended "absent" state, and index-existence checks use explicit === -1.

sugestoes.texto: The invalidation check evaluates the original provider through the organization-aware getById wrapper rather than its stored enabled flag. If a public enabled provider is cached, its organization is disabled, and an administrator sets hideOnLogin=true, the original predicate is false because the organization is disabled and the updated predicate is false because hideOnLogin is true; invalidation is skipped, so re-enabling the organization displays the now-hidden provider from the stale login query. Fetch the original model directly from idpDelegate for login-membership comparison so it uses the same stored-state semantics as the JPA login query.

The cleanup registered for each created provider removes the literal alias "alias" instead of that provider's alias, and the same mistake is repeated for idp-alias-20. TestCleanup ignores the resulting removal failures, leaving realm-level providers behind and contaminating subsequent tests or repeated executions with duplicate aliases and incorrect provider counts. Register cleanup using addIdentityProviderAlias(idpRep.getAlias()) at both creation sites.

The loop creates providers named `idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-19`, but every cleanup action removes the literal alias `alias`. Consequently these actions leave the created providers behind (and can instead remove an unrelated provider or fail on a nonexistent alias). The same mismatch occurs for `idp-alias-20` at line 425. Capture the actual created alias in each cleanup registration.

All getForLogin calls discard the returned stream and assert only internal cache contents. The implementation populates the cache eagerly, before resolving IDs and returning the providers, so replacing its final return with Stream.empty() would still pass this entire test. Consume the returned streams and assert the expected provider IDs or aliases, including a second call for an already-cached search, so the test verifies that cached login lookups actually return the correct providers.

Expanding an existing query carries forward its old organization results but assigns them a fresh revision. For example, request A reads query Q containing organization X; request B changes a provider's login eligibility in X and invalidates Q; A then invalidates the key, loads organization Y, and constructs a new query using Q's stale X results. Publishing with the current counter can accept that new query despite B's completed invalidation. Subsequent logins for X then use stale membership indefinitely (including omitting newly enabled providers). Do not carry forward an old query unless its original revision is still valid; alternatively load only the requested search result into a fresh query and use a revision/counter captured before the read.

issues.descricao: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.
issues.textoGolden: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup registers `identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` inside the loop, and also for idp-alias-20. "alias" is a literal string rather than the actual IDP alias, so none of the created IDPs is ever cleaned up. Use the real alias (e.g. the loop's alias variable / "idp-alias-20") when registering the cleanup. As written, the 21 leaked providers can skew later tests that count IDPs or login caches.

The cleanup is registered for the literal alias "alias" rather than the IDP just created ("idp-alias-" + i). The 20 created IDPs are never removed, and the same applies to the cleanup at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". Use the actual alias, e.g. get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove, so the IDPs don't leak into other tests.

The cleanup registered here uses the literal alias "alias", but the provider just created has alias "idp-alias-" + i. The same mismatch is repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". The cleanup can never find/remove the created providers (null dereference/404 on remove, or at best a silent no-op), so none of the 21 IDPs this test creates are cleaned up and the realm is left polluted for later tests. Use the actual alias, e.g. `testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove` and `get("idp-alias-20")::remove`.

issues.descricao: On a partial cache miss getForLogin merges the previously read login query into a newly revisioned entry, so a concurrent invalidation can be lost and stale IDP IDs for other organizations persist.

comentarios.texto: Do not merge the previously read query into a newly revisioned entry without verifying its revision. A reader can obtain a query containing organization A's IDs, then another transaction disables a provider or changes its organization and invalidates this key. When the reader requests an uncached organization B, this branch obtains a fresh revision but copies the old A results into the new query and publishes it using the current counter. Subsequent A requests receive stale membership indefinitely (a disabled or moved provider still exists, so the null-ID fallback does not repair it). Rebuild rather than copy after invalidation, or ensure the old query's revision is still valid atomically before publishing the merged entry.

issues.descricao: Login-cache invalidation on update compares the organization-aware enabled state, so changing a broker to private while its organization is disabled skips invalidation and leaves the now-private IDP in the cached login list.

comentarios.texto: The early return compares the original IDP's organization-aware enabled state rather than the persisted enabled state used to populate the login cache. If a cached public IDP's organization is disabled and an admin changes BROKER_PUBLIC to false, the original predicate is false because the organization is disabled and the updated predicate is false because the broker is private, so the stale ID remains cached; re-enabling the organization displays the now-private broker because the login bean only rechecks isEnabled. Compare raw persisted models for login-cache invalidation, for example by loading the original through idpDelegate.getById before applying this predicate.

issues.descricao: The LoginFilter javadoc still claims its constants are all criteria for login availability although getLoginPredicate now also checks organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC.

comentarios.texto: getLoginPredicate now also filters on organization link plus the BROKER_PUBLIC config (line 254), but the enum's javadoc directly above (lines 215-217) still states that the enum "contains all fields that are considered when deciding if a provider should be available for login or not", presenting ENABLED/LINK_ONLY/HIDE_ON_LOGIN as the exhaustive criteria. Any reader — or a future LoginFilter constant added against that documented assumption — will believe organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC play no role. Update the javadoc to include the organization-link/public-broker condition, or move the condition into a documented LoginFilter constant.

issues.descricao: The login-cache test creates only public org-linked IDPs, so the new BROKER_PUBLIC check in getLoginPredicate is not covered.

comentarios.texto: Test fixture never covers the new BROKER_PUBLIC branch: all org-linked IDPs are created public, so reverting the getLoginPredicate public-check leaves all counts unchanged and the test still passes. Add at least one org-linked non-public (BROKER_PUBLIC false/missing) enabled IDP and assert it is excluded from getForLogin counts.

issues.descricao: The test never consumes or asserts getForLogin's returned providers and never repeats a query, so the cache-hit path that builds the result is untested and could return wrong IDPs without failing.

comentarios.texto: Consume and assert the results of getForLogin, including a repeat query for the same mode/organization to exercise a cache hit. All calls in this test discard the returned stream and assert only IdentityProviderListQuery contents. The implementation populates that query before reconstructing the returned models, so returning an empty stream (or the wrong providers) at line 254 would still pass the entire test. Assert the expected provider identities on both the initial query and the cached query, rather than only the internal cached count.

issues.descricao: Claims getForLogin re-enters the caching layer by calling session.identityProviders().getById instead of idpDelegate.getById; this deliberately resolves IDs through the per-IDP cache.
issues.textoGolden: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.

issues.descricao: Claims the cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw, non-organization-aware models; getById already wraps them.

comentarios.texto: Cache-hit path in getForLogin returns raw getById results without createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel applied on miss/fallback paths, changing the return-shape contract by cache state. Wrap hit-path results the same way before returning.

The new getForLogin override wraps results with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel on every non-cached path (lines 218 and 249) but the cache-hit loop adds the raw model returned by session.identityProviders().getById(id) directly. Any consumer that relies on the organization-aware model (as documented by the 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped' comment added in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean) therefore receives a different model shape whenever the list happens to be served from cache. Add .map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel) (or wrap before adding to the set) in this loop so the returned shape is identical on cache hit and cache miss.

issues.descricao: Claims linking/unlinking an IDP to an organization never invalidates the getForLogin caches; the org provider routes through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update which does.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The new getForLogin cache (keyed by realm+FetchMode via cacheKeyForLogin) is only invalidated from this provider's create/remove/update methods, but linking/unlinking an IDP to/from an organization is performed by InfinispanOrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider (model/infinispan/.../organization/InfinispanOrganizationProvider.java:249-270), which only calls registerOrganizationInvalidation(organization) and never registers cacheKeyForLogin invalidation. WHY: After an org-link mutation that does not itself route through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update(), the ORG_ONLY and ALL login caches keep returning the pre-mutation ID set, so the login page shows an IDP linked to (or no longer linked to) an organization until some unrelated update/create/remove happens to invalidate the key. HOW: Register cacheKeyForLogin invalidation for all FetchMode values from the organization provider's addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider (or ensure those paths delegate through the IDP storage provider's update so registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate runs).

WHAT: Login cache invalidations only fire from IdP create/update/remove, with no invalidation when an IdP is linked/unlinked to an organization via OrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider. WHY: getForLogin results depend on organizationId/BROKER_PUBLIC, so linking/unlinking leaves the cached ID sets in IdentityProviderListQuery stale and login pages show/hide the wrong brokers until eviction.

issues.descricao: Claims resolving cached IDs one by one with getById turns login listing into N lookups; those lookups hit the per-IDP cache by design.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Cached getForLogin() resolves every cached internalId with an individual session.identityProviders().getById(id) call in a loop. WHY: Turns one login-broker listing (hot login path) into N per-ID lookups, O(N) growth with broker count with per-miss DB fallback and invalidation retry.

issues.descricao: Claims the HashSet in cached getForLogin returns IDPs in nondeterministic order; every caller sorts the result.

comentarios.texto: getForLogin accumulates the login IDPs into `new HashSet<>()` and returns `identityProviders.stream()`. A HashSet provides no iteration-order guarantee, so the cached path returns the IDPs in arbitrary/hash order, unlike the delegate path and the non-cached branch which preserve the delegate's ordering. Any caller of getForLogin that does not re-sort now receives non-deterministic ordering for cached results (and it can differ between cache-hit and cache-miss). Preserve the delegate order (e.g. use a LinkedHashSet and iterate the cached ids in their stored order, or sort the result) so the cached and non-cached paths are consistent.

issues.descricao: Claims remove() of a nonexistent alias now dereferences null; the new login invalidation is null-safe and the other call is unchanged pre-existing code.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remove() stores idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) in storedIdp and calls registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) when the alias key is invalid without a null check. WHY: Removing a non-existent alias causes null dereference on idp.getInternalId() instead of a clean false return.

issues.descricao: Claims getLoginPredicate can NPE on a null config; config is always initialized.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: getLoginPredicate() dereferences idp.getConfig().get(...) without null-checking getConfig(). WHY: A model with null config throws NPE inside the predicate used by create/remove/update invalidation and cached filtering, crashing the invalidation path.

issues.descricao: Claims org-specific ALL/ORG_ONLY login queries include non-public org IDPs, so the BROKER_PUBLIC gate misses invalidations; the query always requires BROKER_PUBLIC=true.

comentarios.texto: getLoginPredicate now declares an org-linked IDP to be a login IDP only when BROKER_PUBLIC is true (`idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`). This predicate is the sole gate for login-cache invalidation: create/remove call registerIDPLoginInvalidation(idp) and update calls registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated), both of which skip invalidating the `.idp.login.<FetchMode>` caches whenever the predicate says the IDP is not a login IDP. However, FetchMode.ALL/ORG_ONLY for a specific organization are the org's own login view and include the organization's linked IDPs regardless of BROKER_PUBLIC (BROKER_PUBLIC only controls the realm-level page). A non-public, org-linked IDP is therefore treated as non-login and its creation/removal/enable-disable/move-into-org does not invalidate the login caches, so those caches keep serving the stale set of IDPs for the org. The predicate's org/BROKER_PUBLIC condition needs to be scoped to the fetch modes it actually applies to (realm-level membership), or the invalidation must be driven by the full set of IDs each mode can return.

The login-cache invalidation is gated exclusively by getLoginPredicate(), which (newly, server-spi IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254) treats an org-linked IDP as a login IDP only when BROKER_PUBLIC is true. But the cache this method guards, produced by getForLogin() (same file, lines 214-255), stores for ORG_ONLY/ALL the ids of the org's own IDPs (as used with a concrete organizationId in OrganizationCacheTest line 406), which can include org-linked non-public broker IDPs. For such an IDP, both original and updated fail the predicate, so registerIDPLoginInvalidation() and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() skip invalidation (the latter via its early `!test(original) && !test(updated)` return), leaving the ORG_ONLY/ALL cache entries stale when the IDP's public/hideOnLogin flag is toggled or its org link is directly reassigned; getForLogin()'s null-id self-heal only catches deletions, not these membership changes. comentarios.texto: Recovery-code verification compares the submitted credential against each stored code with `key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse())`, a short-circuiting, non-constant-time String comparison. Use a constant-time comparison (e.g. MessageDigest.isEqual on the byte arrays, or the same constant-time helper used elsewhere for credential verification) for each candidate instead of String.equals.

The new recovery-code validator uses String.equals to compare a stored secret with attacker-supplied input. This comparison is not constant-time, and anyMatch additionally stops at the first matching code, making validation timing dependent on secret data. Even though this is a testsuite provider, it implements an actual authentication validator and exercises the newly added federation path. Compare fixed-length byte representations with a constant-time primitive and evaluate all candidate codes without short-circuiting.

issues.descricao: website_name compares hostnames case-sensitively, so an uppercase website host matching the instance domain shows only the host instead of the full path.

comentarios.texto: The new `website_name` compares two domain names case-sensitively. `URI(website.to_s).host` preserves the letter case written by the user, whereas `Discourse.current_hostname` is the canonical lower-cased host, and no side is down-cased before the comparison at lines 141, 144-146 and 149 (including the `ends_with?` suffix check). Because DNS host names are case-insensitive identity values, `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` and `http://example.com/user` denote the same host but take different branches, so the same-site check is decided by letter case: the wrong arm is chosen and the full-path form is dropped. Hostname comparisons are case-sensitive even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. issues.descricao: website_name is not marked untrusted, so the host/path of a TL0 user's website, which is hidden from anonymous viewers, is still exposed through the new field.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: website_name re-exposes the user's website for profiles where it is intentionally hidden — the attribute is added to the public `attributes` list (line 43) but not to `untrusted_attributes`, and `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` instead of `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.
